transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see us today?

I've been feeling extremely depressed and empty for the past two months, and my thoughts just feel completely jumbled and hard to put together. On top of that, for about eight months, I've been hearing strange voices and constantly feeling like people are watching me. It's just... really hard to function.
Can you tell me more about when these voices and feelings of being watched started, and how they relate to your periods of feeling depressed and empty?

The voices and the feeling of being watched started about eight months ago, and they were happening completely on their own for a long time. It was only about two months ago that the heavy depression and emptiness set in. Now, I'm dealing with both the voices, the feeling of being watched, and the depression all at the same time.
Did you have any periods where the voices or feeling of being watched went away for a significant time, or have they been consistently present over the past eight months?

They have been consistently present every single day for the past eight months without any breaks. Even during those first six months before the depression started, the voices and the feeling of being watched never went away.
How have these symptoms, particularly the voices and feeling of being watched, affected your daily life, work, or relationships over the past eight months?

The voices and the constant feeling of being watched have made it so I have no motivation to do my daily tasks or work anymore. I've also completely pulled away from my family and friends because I just don't feel safe around anyone and prefer to be left alone. It has made managing my normal life feel almost impossible.

Can you estimate how much of the past eight months you've spent experiencing depressive symptoms, and whether there were any periods where you felt relatively normal or only experienced psychotic symptoms without significant depression?

I have only been experiencing the depressive symptoms for the last two months of the eight-month total. For the first six months, I was dealing with the voices and the feeling of being watched, but my mood was relatively normal. So, most of that early period was just the voices and paranoia without the depression.
During the two months you've been experiencing depressive symptoms, have you had any periods where your mood improved significantly, or has the depression been consistently severe?
No, my mood hasn't improved at all over the past two months. I have felt constantly sad and depressed every single day without any breaks. It has just been a continuous, heavy weight the entire time.

For the six months before the depression started, did you experience any notable impairment in social or occupational functioning solely due to the voices and feeling of being watched, or was it relatively manageable?

No, it wasn't manageable at all and caused a lot of problems. The voices and the constant feeling of being watched made me lose all motivation to do my daily tasks, and I completely withdrew from my friends and social life during those six months.

Can you think of any times during the past eight months when you had a period of at least two weeks where you didn't experience any depressive symptoms, but still had the voices and feeling of being watched, and if so, how did you function during those times?

Yes, during the first six months, I had the voices and paranoia without any depression for weeks at a time. I was terrified and struggling to cope with those fears, but I didn't have the heavy sadness, lack of motivation, or sleep issues that began recently.

During those periods where you had the voices and feeling of being watched without depressive symptoms, were you able to maintain any semblance of normal life, such as working, socializing, or taking care of yourself, or was your functioning still significantly impaired?

Even without the depression, my functioning was still highly impaired and far from normal. I struggled significantly with basic self-care and daily tasks because I had a severe lack of motivation to do anything. On top of that, I completely avoided interacting with others or socializing because I had absolutely no interest in doing so.

So, to confirm, you've had continuous psychotic symptoms for eight months, with a significant portion of that time, about six months, spent with psychotic symptoms but without depressive symptoms, and the last two months with both psychotic and depressive symptoms; is that a correct summary of your experience?

Yes, that is exactly correct. I have been experiencing the voices and feeling of being watched for about eight months in total, but the severe depressive feelings only started about two months ago. That means I had about six months of just dealing with those voices and fears before the heavy depression set in.

However, the key factor that keeps both diagnoses in consideration is the significant duration of psychotic symptoms independent of the depressive episode. The patient's experience of psychotic symptoms for a substantial period before the onset of depressive symptoms suggests Schizophrenia, but the concurrent presence of depressive symptoms for the last two months also supports the consideration of Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type). Further evaluation is needed to determine the primary diagnosis, hence the candidates remain the same.
